findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, House Second Reading
findings.note: On his member vote list, Biggs is recorded Aye on second reading of HB 958 (Election Law Changes). The ratified bill requires county boards to process a voter registration only if the applicant affirmatively states US citizenship (new G.S. 163-83). It requires DMV staff to proceed with a registration only after the applicant states citizenship. It sets a 30-day notice, with a sworn citizenship statement, for forms with no citizenship answer. It also directs the State Board of Elections to set up a process for removing voters flagged as possibly non-citizens by a federal database, and to remove deceased voters from the rolls. Bill page: https://www.ncleg.gov/BillLookUp/2025/H958 ; text: https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, M11 Concur (House vote H-801, 62-47)
findings.note: On his member vote list, Biggs is recorded Aye on the House vote to concur in the Senate committee substitute of HB 958 (final House passage, 62-47). The bill was ratified 2026-08-06 and vetoed by the Governor 2026-08-17. Its last listed action is placed on the House calendar for 2026-09-02 (override status not checked).

findings.motion: HB 475 State ID Cards for High School Students, filed and referred to committee
findings.note: Biggs is a primary sponsor of HB 475, which lets residents aged 16 get a state special identification card and sets up a pilot to issue the cards to public high school students in four counties, including his home county of Randolph. The bill text does not mention voting. It is on file because it concerns access to a state ID. The bill stayed in committee.
